source.quote: FiiO's own parameters page, read 2026-11-24. « Hardware solution »: « SoC: ESP32-S3, DAC: FIIO-developed R2R DAC, USB decoding: XU316, AMP: OPA1642*2+TPA6120A *2 ». « Max. supported sampling rate » rows: « USB decoding: 384kHz/32bit; DSD256 »; « Coaxial decoding: 192kHz/24bit; DSD64 »; « Optical decoding: 192kHz/24bit ». The rate block is headed « Max. supported sampling rate (PEQ=OFF) ». An « Oversampling setting » row reads « OS/NOS ». Bluetooth row: « Bluetooth receiving (5.4) », codecs « SBC/AAC/LDAC ».

facts.chip: « FIIO-developed R2R DAC » - the maker's own ladder, no part number, with an XMOS XU316 as USB receiver.

device_settings.why: « Oversampling setting: OS/NOS ». A two-position switch, stated as a specification row rather than buried in copy. In OS the device applies its own oversampling; in NOS it runs at the rate it is given. Auto exists to do that work with a filter we designed and can account for, so the device's stage belongs out of the path. This is also what makes correctable true: the field applies « only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM ».

_les_plafonds_sont_donnes_PEQ_eteint: The rate rows are headed « Max. supported sampling rate (PEQ=OFF) ». The ceilings are therefore stated for a device whose parametric equaliser is OFF, and the maker says elsewhere on its own pages that PEQ is not applied to every path. This catalogue has no way to attach a CONDITION to a ceiling: pcm_max_hz is one number. Recorded because a user running PEQ may not get these figures, and the page is honest enough to say so in its own heading.
_un_ladder_a_moins_cher_que_tout_ce_que_: « FIIO-developed R2R DAC » in a desktop unit beside the ES9039Q2M-based K13, same chassis, same amplifier, same price class. Every other ladder in this catalogue is a high-end product - Rockna, MSB, Holo, Denafrips, Totaldac, Yggdrasil. This one and the K11 R2R are the first mass-market ladders here, and they arrive with the NOS switch that makes a correction profile possible. If per-device correction is ever going to reach a real number of listeners, it is through parts like these and not through a 20,000 EUR converter.
_loptique_a_192_et_non_96: « Optical decoding: 192kHz/24bit », against 96 kHz on the K13, the K11 R2R, the K11 and the K17 - the same maker, the same chassis family. vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low exists because five makers rate optical at 96; here the SAME maker rates it at 192 on one model and 96 on its sibling. The default is a convention, not a property of TOSLINK, and this pair is the cleanest evidence of it in the catalogue.
